quorum.removalOfLastMemberGuidance.value: "Recreating a single-member control plane is a restore, not a removal: take a snapshot, recreate the node, restore. See docs/runbooks/talos-upgrade.md."

health.vocabulary.absent.value: "A member OF etcd's own membership that did not answer. It is still in the member list, so it is an expected member, it counts toward quorum arithmetic, and `absences-are-declared` can see it."

health.vocabulary.unrepresented.value: "A configured control-plane address with NO member in etcd's membership at all. It is NOT an expected member, so it is invisible to every condition scoped to the member list, including `absences-are-declared`. Only a condition that compares membership size against the derived count can see it: `membership-accounts-for-expected` at the resume entry, `member-count` at preflight and completion."

health.vocabulary.whyItMatters.value: "A removal makes its target unrepresented, which is why the resumed shape cannot require `member-count`. Under the earlier sequential reading `whole` ran first and caught a second unrepresented address by accident; exclusive entry removed that backstop from the resumed shape, so the resumed shape names its own condition rather than relying on a gate it no longer passes through (MCAA-407)."

health.conditions.member-count.rule.value: "The number of members in etcd's own membership (health.memberSetSource) equals the count derived from the control-plane address keys (controlPlane.countKeyPattern), and every one of those members answered. The derived count is the expectation; etcd's membership is the observation. A consumer that counts only the endpoints it chose to dial has not evaluated this condition, it has restated its own input."

health.conditions.quorum-present.rule.value: "The number of members that answered is at least quorum(count), and the number of members in etcd's membership that did not answer is at most maxUnavailable(count), both taken from the quorum table for the derived count. This is the condition that consumes the quorum rule; without it the table is data no predicate reads."

health.conditions.absences-are-declared..value: "Every expected member that is absent (vocabulary.absent — in the member list and did not answer) is a declared target of the operation in progress. An unexplained absence is a second failure the operator did not ask for, and is never tolerated by any predicate — one target absent is a procedure in flight, one target plus one stranger is a degraded cluster. This condition is scoped to the member list, so it says nothing about an unrepresented address; that is `membership-accounts-for-expected`."

health.conditions.membership-accounts-fo.value: "The number of members in etcd's own membership, plus the number of control-plane addresses that are unrepresented -- every unrepresented address, not only the ones this operation declared -- equals the count derived from the control-plane address keys, and every unrepresented address is a declared target of this operation. Two clauses, because the condition refuses on two different observations and owes a different message for each. Stated as one clause over the declared targets alone it fails open: a stranger member, one etcd reports at an address the ConfigSet does not list, cancels an undeclared unrepresented address in the arithmetic and the sum comes out right on a cluster carrying both faults at once -- reproduced at counts 5 and 7 (MCAA-483). The first clause is what sees the stranger; the second is what bounds the relaxation to the target. This is the only condition that can see an unrepresented address on a run that does not evaluate `member-count`: \"expected member\" means a member of the membership, so an address already removed from it is not an absence `absences-are-declared` can detect. On the fresh shape both clauses are implied by `member-count`, which demands the membership be complete; the resumed shape cannot demand that and needs this instead."

health.conditions.no-errors.rule.value: "No member reports a non-empty ERRORS field."

health.conditions.no-learners.rule.value: "No member is a learner. A learner does not vote and does not count toward quorum."

health.conditions.raft-index-converged.r.value: "Every member's RAFT INDEX is within `raftIndexTolerance` of the highest observed index. Members are queried at slightly different moments on a cluster that keeps writing, so exact equality is not a usable gate; a member many indices behind is still catching up and must not be counted as caught up."

health.predicates.whole.summary.value: "Every expected member is present and converged."

health.predicates.whole.rule.value: "The gate for entering and for leaving a destructive procedure. Nothing is destroyed unless the cluster was whole beforehand, and the procedure is not reported successful until it is whole again."

health.predicates.survivable.summary.value: "Quorum holds, every member that answered is converged, and the only members absent or unrepresented are the ones this operation declared it would take away."

health.predicates.survivable.rule.value: "The gate at the revalidation point and on resume, where the target is already gone or about to be. It is weaker than `whole` in exactly one way — it tolerates the declared target being absent or unrepresented — and no weaker in any other: an absent member that is not a declared target, more absences than maxUnavailable, or a control-plane address unrepresented that nobody declared, is unsafe, and every member that did answer must satisfy every other condition. `membership-accounts-for-expected` is what bounds the relaxation to the declared target rather than to any address the membership happens not to list."

health.predicates.survivable.resumeSeman.value: "This is what makes the idempotent re-run decidable. After a crash between \"member removed\" and \"node rejoined\", the target is unrepresented and declared, so `survivable` holds and the run resumes at the next step. If some other member is absent, or some other configured address is unrepresented, `survivable` fails and the run refuses — which is correct, because that cluster has a failure the operator has not seen yet. A guard an operator must bypass to finish a legitimate recovery is not a guard; a guard that consents because the second fault happens to be in the sense it cannot see is not one either."

evaluation.points.preflight.rule.value: "Before anything is drained, tainted, removed or destroyed, on a run whose declared target is still a member. Entered INSTEAD OF `resume`, never before it."

evaluation.points.before-destructive-ste.value: "Immediately before the member removal, with the outgoing member declared as the target. Re-evaluated here even if preflight passed seconds ago."

evaluation.points.resume.rule.value: "On a re-run that finds the declared target already unrepresented — no member for it in etcd's membership at all (health.vocabulary.unrepresented). Entered INSTEAD OF `preflight`: the cluster is short a member at this point by construction, so `whole` is unsatisfiable and evaluating it here would refuse every legitimate recovery. The run skips the removal and continues; it never removes a second member."

evaluation.points.completion.rule.value: "After the replacement rejoins. Success means the cluster is whole again, not that a kubelet reported Ready. Reached by both run shapes."

evaluation.deadDeclaredTargetGuidance.value: "The node to be recreated is still an etcd member but is not answering, so the cluster is not whole and this fresh run refuses. Remove the dead member first (`talosctl -n <surviving-cp> etcd remove-member <id>`), which leaves the target unrepresented, then re-run: the guard enters at `resume` and finishes the recreate without removing a second member. See docs/runbooks/talos-upgrade.md."

evaluation.runShapes.fresh.when.value: "The declared target is still a member of etcd's own membership."

evaluation.runShapes.resumed.when.value: "The declared target is already unrepresented in etcd's own membership."
